chunks: Ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Habib al-Sijistani, who said:

I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who cut off the two right hands of two men. He said, “O Habib, his right hand is cut off for the man whose right hand he cut off first, and his left hand is cut off for the one whose right hand he cut off last, because he only cut off the hand of the latter man while his right hand is retaliation for the first man.”

I said: “Amir al-Muʾminin عليه السلام used only to cut off the right hand and the left foot.” He said, “He only did that in matters that are due from the rights of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. But as for the rights of the Muslims, O Habib, their rights are taken for them in full: a hand for a hand in retaliation when the cutter has a hand, and a foot for a hand when the cutter does not have two hands.”

I said to him: “Is blood money not imposed upon him, and his foot left for him?” He said, “Blood money is only imposed upon him if he cuts off a man’s hand and the cutter has neither two hands nor two feet. Then blood money is imposed upon him, because he has no limb from which retaliation may be taken.”

key_terms.جَارِحَةٌ: a limb from which retaliatory punishment may be exacted
key_terms.حُقُوقُ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ: the personal rights and claims of injured Muslims
key_terms.حُقُوقِ ٱللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: divinely mandated rights and penalties belonging to Allah
key_terms.قِصَاصُ ٱلْيَدِ بِٱلْيَدِ: retaliation by taking a hand for a hand
key_terms.ٱلدِّيَةُ: financial compensation owed when direct retaliation cannot be carried out
key_terms.ٱلرِّجْلُ ٱلْيُسْرَى: the left foot, mentioned in contrast with certain punishments
key_terms.ٱلْيَدُ ٱلْيُمْنَى: the right hand as the primary limb discussed in retaliation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of qisas if someone cuts off the right hands of two people?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on qisas in cases where a person severs the right hands of two different men. It distinguishes between the rights of Allah and the rights of people, stating that in private injury claims retaliation is taken as fully as possible from the offender’s remaining limbs, and diyah is only required when no limb remains for qisas.
